lessons.title: Tense accuracy: routines, current work and past events
objectives: Choose a tense from the meaning and time context.
Keep auxiliaries and main verb forms consistent.
lessons.explanationRomanUrdu: Tense sirf aik time word dekh kar nahin chunte; dekhen baat routine hai, abhi jari kaam hai ya mukammal past event. Present Simple routine, Present Continuous aarzi jari kaam aur Past Simple finished past ke liye use hota hai. Sawal aur nafi mein auxiliary ke baad verb ki form bhi durust rakhen.
rulesRomanUrdu: Routine: She usually works at home. Aarzi kaam: She is working in the office this week.
Finished past: She worked in the office yesterday. Did/did not ke baad base form: Did she work?
Do/does ke saath base verb: Does he work? He does not work.
Know aur believe jaisay state verbs ko is basic meaning mein aam tor par continuous nahin banate: I know the answer.

reading.text: Mina usually works at home, where she writes short reports for a community club. This week, she is working in the club office because the team is preparing an exhibition. Yesterday, she checked the visitor information and corrected two room numbers. She did not change the opening time. A colleague asks, “Do you usually work here?” Mina explains that this is a temporary arrangement. Her answer changes tense because she is describing a routine, current work and a finished event, rather than three actions at the same time.
reading.meaningRomanUrdu: Mina aam tor par ghar se community club ki reports likhti hai. Is hafte exhibition ki tayari ke liye club office mein kaam kar rahi hai. Kal visitor information dekhi aur do room numbers durust kiye; opening time nahin badla. Saathi poochta hai kya aam tor par yahin kaam karti ho. Woh batati hai yeh aarzi arrangement hai. Routine, ab kaam aur kal ka mukammal event alag tenses mangte hain.

lessons.title: Present Perfect and Past Simple: experience and detail
objectives: Move from an undated experience to a finished past detail.
Use gone and been in a clear context.
lessons.explanationRomanUrdu: Present Perfect tajurba ya ab tak ki halat ko guzre hue exact waqt ke baghair jorta hai. Finished past detail den to Past Simple use karen. I have been to ka yahan matlab ja kar wapas aa chuka hai; has gone to ke context mein shakhs abhi gaya hua hai.
rulesRomanUrdu: Have you ever visited ...? se ab tak ka tajurba poochte hain.
When did you go? / I went last year se finished detail milti hai.
I have lived here for three years continuing state hai; I lived there in 2020 finished period hai.
She has gone to the library: woh abhi wahan gayi hui hai. She has been to the library: daura kar ke wapas aa chuki hai, is context mein.

reading.text: “Have you ever visited a science museum?” Ali asks. Sara has visited several, but she chooses one clear example. “I went to a small museum last year,” she says. “I saw an exhibition about everyday inventions.” Ali asks whether her brother can join their next visit. Sara explains that he has gone to another town and is still there, so he cannot come today. She has been to that town herself, but she returned last week. Their conversation moves between experience, a finished visit and a present situation.
reading.meaningRomanUrdu: Ali museum jane ka tajurba poochta hai. Sara kai museum ja chuki hai lekin pichhle saal ka aik daura batati hai. Us ne aam ijadaat ki exhibition dekhi thi. Bhai agle daure mein aa sakta hai ya nahin? Woh doosre shehar gaya hua hai aur abhi wahin hai. Sara us shehar ja kar pichhle hafte wapas aa chuki hai. Guftagu mein tajurba, finished visit aur maujooda halat alag hain.

lessons.title: Narrative tenses: background and main events
objectives: Set a past scene with Past Continuous.
Move a story forward with Past Simple events.
lessons.explanationRomanUrdu: Kahani mein background batata hai ke us waqt kya jari tha. Past Continuous se scene aur Past Simple se main events batayen. While do saath jari actions jor sakta hai; when aik chhote event ko background ke saath jor sakta hai.
rulesRomanUrdu: Background: We were waiting outside the hall.
Main event: A volunteer opened the door.
Interrupted action: I was reading when the lights went out.
While I was speaking, she was taking notes do saath jari actions hain; har past verb ko continuous banana zaroori nahin.

reading.text: We were waiting outside the exhibition hall, and a few visitors were looking at a map. While my friend was checking our tickets, a volunteer arrived. He explained that the main entrance was closed and showed us another door. We followed him through a quiet courtyard. Meanwhile, another volunteer was arranging chairs inside. When we reached the room, the talk had not started, so we found seats near the front. The scene describes what was happening, while the shorter actions move the story from the entrance to the room.
reading.meaningRomanUrdu: Hum exhibition hall ke bahar intezar kar rahe the; kuch visitors naqsha dekh rahe the. Dost tickets check kar raha tha ke volunteer aaya. Main darwaza band tha is liye doosra dikhaya. Hum sehan se us ke peeche gaye. Isi dauran andar kursiyan lag rahi thin. Kamre mein pohanche to talk shuru nahin hui thi aur aage baith gaye. Jari actions scene aur chhote actions kahani ko aage barhate hain.

lessons.title: Past Perfect: an earlier event in a past story
objectives: Show that one past event happened before another.
Form had + past participle and had not.
lessons.explanationRomanUrdu: Past Perfect kisi past point se bhi pehle mukammal hue action ko wazeh karta hai. Pattern har subject ke liye had + past participle hai. Har purane event ko Past Perfect banana zaroori nahin; sequence wazeh ho to Past Simple kafi ho sakta hai.
rulesRomanUrdu: When I arrived, the talk had started: talk pehle shuru hui.
Had ke baad participle: had gone, had seen, had finished.
Negative: We had not booked seats before we arrived.
Question: Had you checked the time? Earlier event ke baad main timeline aam tor par Past Simple mein jari reh sakti hai.

Pehle ke actions das baje ki halat ki wajah batate hain; phir main kahani jari hoti hai. Yeh farzi schedule hai.

lessons.explanationRomanUrdu: Future ke liye aik hi form har maqsad par lazim nahin. Kuch contexts mein aik se zyada form mumkin ho sakti hai; yahan wazeh situations par practice hai.

lessons.explanationRomanUrdu: Used to + base verb pehle ke mamool ya state ke liye hai jo ab mukhtalif ho. I used to walk to work batata hai ke pehle yeh routine tha. Is ko be used to + noun/-ing se na milayen; us ka matlab kisi cheez ka aadi hona hai.

Past state: This building used to be a library.
Question: Did you use to live here? Negative: I did not use to live here.
Is lesson mein used to + base verb hai. I am used to walking aik alag structure hai, jis ka matlab walking ka aadi hona hai.

lessons.title: Conditionals: routine results and possible future plans
objectives: Distinguish a repeated result from a possible future result.
Use if and unless without changing the intended condition.
lessons.explanationRomanUrdu: Zero conditional aam result ya routine batata hai: if + present, present. First conditional mumkin future condition aur result batata hai: if + present, will + base verb. Unless ka aam matlab if not hai; is ko extra negative ke saath ghalti se ulta na karen.
rulesRomanUrdu: Routine: If I finish early, I walk home.
Specific future: If I finish early tomorrow, I will walk home.
Unless it rains, we will walk = If it does not rain, we will walk.
Is basic first conditional mein if clause ke andar will nahin. Clause ki jagah badal sakti hai: We will walk if it is dry.

reading.text: Our club usually meets outside. If a meeting finishes early, we walk to the station together. Tomorrow is different because we have a longer workshop. If it finishes before five, we will take the earlier bus. Unless it rains, we will wait in the courtyard. If it rains, we will meet inside instead. These are plans for one future occasion, while the first sentence about walking describes a repeated routine. We agree to send a message if the meeting place changes, so nobody waits at the wrong entrance.
reading.meaningRomanUrdu: Club aam tor par bahar milta hai. Meeting jaldi khatam ho to station saath paidal jate hain; yeh routine hai. Kal lambi workshop hai. Paanch se pehle khatam hui to pehli bus len ge. Barish na hui to sehan mein, hui to andar intezar karen ge. Jagah badli to message bhejen ge. Routine aur aik khaas future din ke plans alag hain.

She explains her own action rather than claiming that she solved every problem alone. When asked about an unfamiliar tool, she says that she has not used it yet and asks what training is available. reading.text: Notice for an imaginary community club: During busy evening sessions, members sometimes wait at the entrance because one volunteer has to check names and answer questions at the same desk. The committee proposes a four-week trial with a separate information table. One volunteer would check names, while another would explain the room layout and the session timetable. The purpose is to reduce waiting and make instructions clearer for new visitors. The proposal does not change the session times or membership arrangements. However, it depends on enough volunteers being available; if there are too few, the usual single-desk system will continue. At the end of four weeks, members and volunteers will be asked whether the new arrangement helped. The committee will then decide whether to keep it, change it or stop it. No total cost is given in this notice. Readers are invited to comment on the proposed arrangement before the trial begins, rather than assume that a permanent change has already been approved.

reading.text: Mina asks Ali to help with an extra evening session. Ali replies, “I would like to help, but I need to check my timetable. I am not sure that I can arrive by six. Could we start at six thirty, or could I join after the introduction?” His words suggest interest and a practical concern about timing. They do not show that he dislikes the group, and they do not give a final promise. Mina agrees to check the later start with the organiser. Both speakers still need to confirm the plan. The inference comes from explicit wording and reasons, not from an assumed private motive.
